extracted.intended_audience: aspiring poets, creative writers, and readers/students of poetic theory
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for poets on what constitutes true poetic power: qualities of imagination, naming, truthfulness, relation to nature, form vs thought, and the poet's life and habits. Applies to composing poetry that is original, representative, and spiritually resonant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet as representative/complete man
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet is representative. He stands among partial men for the complete man, and apprises us not of his wealth, but of the common wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The poet 'receives of the soul as he also receives, but they more' — he traverses the whole scale of experience and is the largest power to receive and impart. Evaluate a poet by how well they speak for wider human experience rather than merely personal skill or display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original announcement (announces what no man foretold)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sign and credentials of the poet are that he announces that which no man foretold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True poetry brings a novel perception or 'new thought'—not mere cleverness of form. Assess whether the work presents genuinely new insight or revelation rather than restating commonplace observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veracity of report / truthfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Of course the value of genius to us is in the veracity of its report. Talent may frolic and juggle; genius realizes and adds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge poetry by its truthfulness — whether the poet's vision rings true and deepens understanding, not merely by ornamentation or rhetorical effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination as high seeing (intellect being where it sees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagination...is a very high sort of seeing, which does not come by study, but by the intellect being where and what it sees; by sharing the path or circuit of things through forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetic imagination should feel like genuine sight or participation in the object rather than learned description. Look for evidence of 'sharing the path' of things; the poem should render the object's inner life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet as namer / language-maker
rubrics_metrics.description: By virtue of this science the poet is the Namer or Language-maker, naming things sometimes after their appearance, sometimes after their essence...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how the poet renames or reframes experience—does diction reveal freshly perceived essences? Words originally were 'strokes of genius'; check whether the language feels inventive and essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thought prior to form; metre-making argument
rubrics_metrics.description: For it is not metres, but a metre-making argument that makes a poem,--a thought so passionate and alive that...it has an architecture of its own. The thought and the form are equal in the order of time, but in the order of genesis the thought is prior to the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether form grows organically from an original idea (a 'metre-making argument') rather than form being an end in itself. Technical finish without a vital thought is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of nature as symbolic language
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature offers all her creatures to him as a picture-language. Being used as a type, a second wonderful value appears in the object...Things admit of being used as symbols because nature is a symbol, in the whole, and in every part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the poet's use of natural imagery as symbolic — symbols should open to larger meanings, not be merely decorative. Ordinary objects should serve as expressive signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal accessibility / commonwealth of poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet stands among partial men for the complete man...All men live by truth and stand in need of expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The poet's work should speak beyond elite tastes and engage common human needs. Consider whether the poem enriches general human understanding and feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resisting mere cultivation/finish over soul
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who are esteemed umpires of taste...if you inquire whether they are beautiful souls...they are selfish and sensual. Their cultivation is local... Their knowledge of the fine arts is some study of rules and particulars...exercised for amusement or for show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware of polished work that lacks inward authenticity. Evaluate whether technical polish serves soul and substance rather than replacing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet as sayer / lover of beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet is the sayer, the namer, and represents beauty...the poet is not any permissive potentate, but is emperor in his own right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the poet by their capacity to 'say' — to render beauty and name things — rather than by social status or action. The poet's primary domain is expressive revelation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to perceive the double/multiple meaning of sensuous facts
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest minds...have never ceased to explore the double meaning, or...much more manifold meaning, of every sensuous fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A poet should discern layered meanings in sensory particulars. Evaluate whether images carry multifaceted significance rather than single, flat readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet's balance: reception and imparting
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet is the person in whom these powers are in balance, the man without impediment, who sees and handles that which others dream of, traverses the whole scale of experience, and is representative of man, in virtue of being the largest power to receive and to impart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both receptive sensitivity and the ability to communicate — a poet must both perceive keenly and transmit that perception effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mean and commonplace as potent symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Small and mean things serve as well as great symbols. The meaner the type by which a law is expressed, the more pungent it is, and the more lasting in the memories of men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the poet can turn ordinary, humble details into powerful symbolic carriers; originality often lies in transforming the commonplace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-attaching things to the Whole; consecration of new facts
rubrics_metrics.description: For as it is dislocation and detachment from the life of God that makes things ugly, the poet, who re-attaches things to nature and the Whole...disposes very easily of the most disagreeable facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the poem restores unity between particular facts and larger meaning, integrating modern or ugly elements into an ordered whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluidity of symbols; avoidance of mystic fixation
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the imagination is to flow, and not to freeze. The difference betwixt the poet and the mystic, that the last nails a symbol to one sense...Mysticism consists in the mistake of an accidental and individual symbol for an universal one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that symbols remain dynamic and adaptable rather than rigidly fixed to a single private meaning; meaning should be generative, not fossilized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspiration requires surrender, not mere technique
rubrics_metrics.description: The condition of true naming, on the poet's part, is his resigning himself to the divine aura which breathes through forms, and accompanying that...he is caught up into the life of the Universe, his speech is thunder, his thought is law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess willingness to abandon strict intellectual control and allow an inspired, participatory mode. Technique must yield to intoxication of insight (not artificial intoxication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purity of life and body over narcotic substitutes
rubrics_metrics.description: The sublime vision comes to the pure and simple soul in a clean and chaste body. That is not an inspiration, which we owe to narcotics...Milton says that the lyric poet may drink wine...but the epic poet...must drink water out of a wooden bowl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate poet's lifestyle insofar as it supports genuine perception: reliance on narcotics or artificial stimulants is criticized as counterfeit. Simplicity and bodily purity are prized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliaries allowed but not substitutes (conversation, art, travel)
rubrics_metrics.description: All men avail themselves of such means as they can...conversation, music, pictures, sculpture, dancing, theatres, travelling, war...are several coarser or finer quasi-mechanical substitutes for the true nectar...These are auxiliaries to the centrifugal tendency of a man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize external aides as useful for stimulating perception, but judge whether the poet relies on them in place of inner vision. They should supplement, not replace, the deeper imaginative faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as immortal progeny (durability of songs)
rubrics_metrics.description: She detaches from him a new self, that the kind may be safe...a fearless, sleepless, deathless progeny...The melodies of the poet ascend and leap and pierce into the deeps of infinite time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the poem aspires to durability — poems whose insight passes into cultural memory are the truest successes; ask whether lines feel generative of enduring meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry must be a new confession for each age
rubrics_metrics.description: The experience of each new age requires a new confession, and the world seems always waiting for its poet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess topical and spiritual freshness: does the poem articulate what its time uniquely requires, rather than recycling earlier confessions?

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet as perceiver of causal/necessary ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: He is a beholder of ideas and an utterer of the necessary and causal...the true poet...is the only teller of news, for he was present and privy to the appearance which he describes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the poet grasps causality and necessity behind phenomena and communicates that understanding with authority, not merely ornamental commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism's legitimation: poems as imperfect transcripts of nature's text
rubrics_metrics.description: The legitimation of criticism, in the mind's faith that the poems are a corrupt version of some text in nature with which they ought to be made to tally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique should aim to restore fidelity to nature's 'text'—assess how closely a poem aligns with or deviates from the perceived natural pattern it attempts to render.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic diction should be musical and fitting
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the truest word ever spoken, and the phrase will be the fittest, most musical, and the unerring voice of the world for that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether diction and phrasing feel organically musical and suited to the truth being expressed, not merely metrically clever or artificially ornate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative economy: few facts, deep significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Why covet a knowledge of new facts? Day and night, house and garden, a few books, a few actions, serve us as well as would all trades and all spectacles. We are far from having exhausted the significance of the few symbols we use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the poet can mine depth from limited material—poetry need not be encyclopedic; economical choice of images used profoundly is preferable to clutter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative liberation as measure of intellect
rubrics_metrics.description: This emancipation is dear to all men, and the power to impart it, as it must come from greater depth and scope of thought, is a measure of intellect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the poet by their ability to emancipate readers' perceptions—works that unlock new ways of seeing indicate intellectual depth and breadth.
